name: Linorobot2
description: A ROS2 software and micro-ROS firmware framework for building DIY mobile robots — not a fixed robot with a bill of materials the way most entries here are. Builders bring their own chassis and a supported menu of microcontrollers, motor drivers, LiDARs, and cameras; the pictured unit is a lab-built Mecanum-wheel robot running Linorobot2 on hardware its own builder sourced and assembled.

sourcing: Specs compiled from the Linorobot2 GitHub repositories, project site, and third-party community/technical write-ups as of this build. Because this is a bring-your-own-hardware framework, exact specs and cost depend entirely on the builder's own component choices — the figures here describe the supported range, not one fixed configuration.

pricing.summary: There is no official reference cost, because Linorobot2 is a framework rather than a product with a bill of materials; a widely-cited community estimate puts a minimal electronics-only configuration at roughly $131, excluding the chassis, motors, wheels, compute board, battery, and any LiDAR or depth camera. A complete build like the one pictured, with a metal enclosure, Mecanum wheels, spinning LiDAR, and a compute SBC, would run well beyond that figure — likely several hundred to over a thousand dollars depending entirely on the components a builder chooses.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The Linorobot2 project itself is genuinely open source (Apache-2.0, ~1,000 GitHub stars, actively maintained).
